```{r}
#| label: setup-ritem
#| include: false
#| cache: false

renv::load("~/Github/longhaiSK.github.io/")

# ==============================================================================
# ALGORITHM & LOGIC OF THE ritem() FUNCTION
# ==============================================================================
# 
# THE PROBLEM: 
# Pandoc (the engine behind Quarto) automatically forces all Markdown numbered 
# lists to count forward (1, 2, 3...), even if you type (10, 9, 8). 
#
# THE SOLUTION (The Two-Pass Algorithm):
# To count backward, the function must know the TOTAL number of items in a list 
# before it prints the first one. Since R executes code linearly top-to-bottom, 
# this requires saving state across two separate document compilations ("knits").
#
# STEP-BY-STEP LOGIC:
# 1. Initialization & Scoping: 
#    The function creates a hidden global environment (`.ritem_env`) to track  
#    state during the knit. It names its memory file (the .rds aux file) based 
#    on the specific .qmd file being compiled. This prevents List A in "CV.qmd" 
#    from accidentally overwriting List B in "Syllabus.qmd".
#
# 2. Loading Previous State (Pass 2): 
#    If the document has been knitted before, it loads `prev_totals` from the  
#    .rds file. This tells the function exactly how many items were in each list 
#    last time.
#
# 3. Handling List Breaks (The "new" signal):
#    If `ritem("new")` is called, it increments the list counter and resets the 
#    item counter to 0. It returns an empty string so it doesn't leave stray 
#    marks in the document.
#
# 4. Counting & Checkpointing (Pass 1):
#    Every time `ritem()` is called for an item, it increments the item counter, 
#    updates `curr_totals` in memory, and immediately saves to the .rds file. 
#    Saving on EVERY call guarantees the final count is preserved even if the 
#    rest of the document fails to compile.
#
# 5. The Reverse Math:
#    It calculates the display number as: (Total Items - Current Item + 1).
#    *Fallback:* If this is the very first time knitting (no `prev_totals`), 
#    it just prints forward (1, 2, 3...) so the document doesn't crash.
#
# 6. Pandoc Bypassing (Output):
#    To stop Pandoc from destroying the reverse numbers, it outputs:
#    `<!-- --> \n\n %d.`
#    The empty HTML comment acts as a brick wall, forcing Pandoc to end the 
#    previous list and start a brand new list precisely at the calculated number.
#    Because this outputs standard Markdown list syntax, 4-space indented 
#    sublists nested underneath it will parse perfectly.
#
# 7. Formatting & Styling (Typst & HTML CSS):
#    Because Pandoc is forced to generate individual list blocks (via <!-- -->),
#    we must manually override the appearance in both output formats to achieve 
#    the [1], [2] style:
#    - TYPST: A custom `#show enum` rule intercepts these generated lists, strips 
#      Pandoc's hardcoded "1." format, applies the "[1]" numbering, and preserves 
#      the reverse `start` number without triggering an infinite recursion loop.
#    - HTML/CSS: Custom CSS overrides Bootstrap's default numbering by hiding 
#      the standard list-style and injecting `content: "[" counter(list-item) "]"` 
#      via the `::marker` pseudo-element. It also strictly manages margins so 
#      4-space indented sublists align perfectly with the parent text.
# ==============================================================================

ritem <- function(n = NULL) {
  # 1. Initialize environment on the very first call per knit session
  if (!exists(".ritem_env", envir = globalenv())) {
    env <- new.env()
    env$list_idx <- 0
    env$item_idx <- 0
    
    input_name <- knitr::current_input()
    if (is.null(input_name)) input_name <- "default"
    env$aux_file <- paste0(".", tools::file_path_sans_ext(input_name), "_ritem.rds")
    
    if (file.exists(env$aux_file)) {
      env$prev_totals <- readRDS(env$aux_file)
    } else {
      env$prev_totals <- numeric(0)
    }
    env$curr_totals <- numeric(0)
    
    assign(".ritem_env", env, envir = globalenv())
  }
  
  env <- get(".ritem_env", envir = globalenv())
  
  # 2. Handle 'new' initialization signal
  if (identical(n, "new")) {
    env$list_idx <- env$list_idx + 1
    env$item_idx <- 0
    if (length(env$curr_totals) < env$list_idx) {
      env$curr_totals[env$list_idx] <- 0
    }
    return(knitr::asis_output(""))
  }
  
  # 3. Handle backwards compatibility if a manual number is passed
  if (is.numeric(n)) {
    env$list_idx <- env$list_idx + 1
    env$item_idx <- 0
    env$prev_totals[env$list_idx] <- n 
  }
  
  # 4. Failsafe if user forgets 'new' for the very first list
  if (env$list_idx == 0) {
    env$list_idx <- 1
    env$item_idx <- 0
  }
  
  # 5. Increment item counter and save progress
  env$item_idx <- env$item_idx + 1
  env$curr_totals[env$list_idx] <- env$item_idx
  
  saveRDS(env$curr_totals, env$aux_file)
  
  # 6. Determine the reversed number to display
  total <- if (length(env$prev_totals) >= env$list_idx && !is.na(env$prev_totals[env$list_idx])) {
    env$prev_totals[env$list_idx]
  } else {
    env$item_idx
  }
  
  num <- total - env$item_idx + 1
  
  # 7. Output Formatting
  out_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to")
  
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    out <- sprintf("\n\n\\hangindent=2.5em \\hangafter=1 \\makebox[2.5em][l]{%d.}", num)
    return(knitr::asis_output(out))
    
  } else if (knitr::is_html_output() || (!is.null(out_format) && out_format == "typst")) {
    # The empty HTML comment forces Pandoc to treat this as a list in BOTH HTML and Typst,
    # ensuring that 4-space sublists are parsed correctly everywhere.
    out <- sprintf("\n\n<!-- -->\n\n%d.", num)
    return(knitr::asis_output(out))
    
  } else {
    return(paste0("\n\n[", num, "]"))
  }
}
```

```{=typst}
// ====================================================================
// TYPST RULES FOR REVERSE LISTS 
// ====================================================================
#show figure: set block(breakable: true)

// 1. Global spacing and indents
#set enum(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.75em)
#set list(indent: 2em, body-indent: 0.75em)

// 2. Nested bullet list rule
#show list: it => { 
  set list(indent: 1em)
  it 
}

// 3. The Numbering Enforcer (with recursion safety)
#show enum: it => { 
  set list(indent: 1em)
  
  // If it already has the right numbering, return it as-is to break the loop
  if it.numbering == "[1]" {
    it
  } else {
    // Otherwise, rebuild the list to strip Pandoc's formatting
    enum(
      numbering: "[1]",
      start: it.start,    // Keeps your reverse number
      ..it.children       // Keeps all the actual items and sublists
    )
  }
}
```

```{=html}
<!-- 
====================================================================
HTML / CSS RULES FOR REVERSE LISTS
==================================================================== 
-->
<style>
  

  /* 5. OVERRIDE BOOTSTRAP NUMBERING to format exactly as [1] */
  ol > li {
    list-style-type: none !important; 
  }

  ol > li::marker {
    content: "[" counter(list-item) "] " !important;
    font-weight: 600;
  }

  /* 6. PROTECT NESTED BULLETS so they retain their standard dots */
  ol ul > li {
    list-style-type: disc !important;
  }
  
  ol ul > li::marker {
    content: normal !important;
  }
</style>
```
